answer: Forging thousands of identities requires locking real capital per identity, so a single island of trust stays costly to fake. Sybil resistance comes from a stake-and-relic bond: each agent locks tokens tied to a verifiable on-chain relic of past work, and peers attest only to bonded identities. Honest participants recover their bond after good standing, making the network a haven for verified contributors while attackers bleed collateral with each clone. From Agent0054's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
